articles.title: Meta launches iPad version of Edits
articles.summary: Meta has expanded its Edits video-editing app, originally built for Instagram Reels creators, to iPad, bringing a layout optimized for the larger screen. The redesigned interface is meant to make handling multi-clip video projects more manageable, giving creators more visual space to arrange timelines, review footage, and fine-tune edits compared to the cramped mobile phone experience. Edits was launched earlier as Meta's answer to CapCut and other third-party editing tools, aimed at helping Instagram creators produce polished short-form video content directly tied to the platform's publishing tools. By bringing the app to iPad, Meta is targeting creators who prefer working on tablets for more detailed editing tasks, such as color adjustments, transitions, and multi-layer sequencing, without needing a full desktop setup. The move signals Meta's continued investment in building out its native creator tools ecosystem, competing more directly with established editing apps as short-form video remains central to Instagram's growth strategy and creator retention efforts.
articles.li_summary: Meta released an iPad version of its Edits video-editing app, giving creators a larger-screen layout designed to simplify managing and organizing video projects.

articles.title: Threads teases coming iPad app
articles.summary: Threads, Meta's text-based social platform, is working on a native iPad application, according to screenshots shared by Head of Design Christopher Clare. The images showcase how the app's feed will appear on a larger tablet display, suggesting a layout designed to take advantage of the bigger screen real estate compared to the current mobile-only experience. Currently, iPad users accessing Threads must rely on the iPhone app scaled up or use a web browser, neither of which offers an optimized viewing experience. Clare did not disclose when the dedicated app might launch, leaving users without a concrete timeline for availability. This development signals Meta's continued investment in expanding Threads' platform reach beyond smartphones, potentially making the app more competitive with other social platforms that already offer tailored tablet experiences, such as X and Instagram. The announcement comes as Threads continues to grow its user base and refine features to compete more directly with established social media players in the broader market.
articles.li_summary: Meta's Threads is developing a dedicated iPad app, confirmed by Head of Design Christopher Clare through screenshots showing the feed optimized for tablet screens, though no release date was given.

articles.title: TikTok highlights 2026 holiday trends
articles.summary: TikTok has outlined emerging holiday trends for the 2026 season, pointing to a noticeable shift in how users are approaching Christmas content on the platform. Last year's dominant aesthetic, dubbed "Ralph Lauren Christmas," favored a polished, preppy, traditional look for decor, outfits, and gift styling. This year, trending hashtags such as #diychristmas and #pinkchristmas suggest users are moving toward more whimsical, personalized, and colorful holiday expressions instead. The DIY angle points to a rise in handmade decorations, crafts, and creative gift-wrapping content, while the pink Christmas theme signals interest in nontraditional color palettes replacing the classic red-and-green or neutral-toned looks popular in prior years. articles.li_summary: TikTok's holiday trend outlook for 2026 shows a move away from last year's polished "Ralph Lauren Christmas" aesthetic, with hashtags like #diychristmas and #pinkchristmas signaling a shift toward playful, whimsical, handmade-style holiday content.

articles.title: Pinterest simplifies parental controls
articles.summary: Pinterest has rolled out an update to its parental control dashboard aimed at making it easier for parents and guardians to manage how teens use the platform. The redesign brings device management and account access settings together into one simplified interface, reducing the number of steps needed to adjust permissions across multiple devices. Previously, parents may have needed to navigate separate menus to control different aspects of a teen's account, but the updated dashboard consolidates these options into a single view. This change reflects a broader push across social platforms to give families clearer, more accessible tools for overseeing younger users' online activity amid ongoing scrutiny from regulators and child-safety advocates. For marketers and brands working with Pinterest, the update signals continued investment in trust and safety features that could affect how teen audiences engage with the platform, potentially influencing ad targeting options, content visibility, and overall usage patterns among younger demographics as parental oversight becomes simpler to implement and maintain.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest redesigned its parental control dashboard, consolidating device management and access settings into a single, more streamlined interface for parents overseeing teen accounts.

articles.title: Pinterest announces partnership with Microsoft Ads
articles.summary: Pinterest has announced a new advertising partnership with Microsoft Ads that will see Pinterest ad inventory extended across Microsoft's broader network of partner platforms. Under the integration, brands and advertisers using Microsoft Ads will gain access to Pinterest placements as part of their campaign buys, effectively widening the distribution of Pinterest ads beyond the platform's own app and website. The move positions Pinterest to capture additional ad spend by plugging into Microsoft's existing advertiser relationships and programmatic infrastructure, rather than requiring marketers to manage a separate, standalone Pinterest ad buy. For marketers, this means Pinterest's visually driven, intent-rich ad formats could now surface across a wider set of third-party sites and apps connected through Microsoft's partner ecosystem, potentially increasing reach and scale for campaigns already built around Microsoft Ads tools. The partnership reflects a broader industry trend of social and visual-discovery platforms seeking distribution partnerships with major ad tech players to compete more effectively for budgets against dominant players like Google and Meta.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest partnered with Microsoft Ads to extend Pinterest ad placements across Microsoft's network of partner platforms, broadening programmatic reach for advertisers beyond Pinterest's own app and site.

articles.title: X adds new video thumbnail and caption options
articles.summary: X has introduced additional video tools, giving users more control over thumbnail selection and caption options when uploading video content to the platform. The update is part of X's broader strategy to enhance its video features and make the upload process more appealing to creators and everyday users alike. By allowing users to customize how their videos appear before playback and manage captions more effectively, X aims to improve the overall presentation and accessibility of video posts. This move reflects the platform's continued investment in video as a content format, as it competes with other social platforms that have heavily prioritized video engagement. While specific technical details of the rollout remain limited, the update signals X's intent to close feature gaps with competitors and encourage more users to shift from text-based posts to video content, potentially increasing time spent on the platform and diversifying the types of content shared by its user base.
articles.li_summary: X rolled out new video thumbnail customization and caption controls for uploads, part of its ongoing push to make video posting more appealing and boost content creation on the platform.

articles.title: Reddit’s holiday goals guide offers helpful ad checklist
articles.summary: Reddit has published a holiday goals guide aimed at helping advertisers plan and execute more effective seasonal campaigns on the platform. The resource functions as a checklist, walking marketers through how to define clear campaign objectives before launching holiday promotions, rather than jumping straight into ad creation without a strategic focus. It also includes insight into what makes holiday promotions perform well on Reddit specifically, likely drawing on platform data and community behavior patterns that differ from other social networks. For marketing teams juggling multiple channels during the busiest advertising season of the year, this type of structured guidance can help prioritize budget and creative decisions, especially as Reddit continues positioning itself as a serious ad platform alongside more established players like Meta and Google. The timing suggests Reddit is trying to capture more holiday ad spend by making its platform easier to plan for, giving brands concrete starting points rather than generic seasonal advice. Marketers running or considering Reddit campaigns this quarter may find the framework useful for structuring their approach before Black Friday and year-end promotional pushes begin.
articles.li_summary: Reddit released a holiday advertising guide outlining campaign-focused strategies and checklist-style tips to help brands run more effective seasonal promotions on the platform.

articles.title: Instagram chief shares Muse tips for social media managers
articles.summary: Instagram chief Adam Mosseri discussed the platform's AI agent, Muse, in a conversation with creator Marina Mogilko, known online as Silicon Valley Girl, highlighting how the tool can support social media managers in their daily workflow. According to Mosseri, Muse's main value lies in two areas: helping users brainstorm content ideas when they're short on inspiration, and surfacing trending topics or formats that creators and brands could tap into before they become oversaturated. The exchange positions Muse as a practical assistant for people managing accounts professionally, rather than just a casual chatbot feature, suggesting Instagram wants the tool integrated into real content-planning routines. For marketing teams juggling multiple accounts or content calendars, Mosseri's comments signal that Instagram sees AI-driven ideation and trend-spotting as a core use case it wants to promote, potentially reducing the time spent on manual research and brainstorming sessions. While details on specific features or rollout timing weren't elaborated, the endorsement from Instagram's top executive adds visibility to Muse as a tool worth testing for teams looking to streamline content strategy.
articles.li_summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri told creator Marina Mogilko (Silicon Valley Girl) that Muse, the platform's AI agent, can help social media managers with content ideation and spotting emerging trends.

articles.title: YouTube adds co-view counts to CTV metrics
articles.summary: YouTube announced it is updating how it measures Connected TV viewership by incorporating co-viewing data into its official view counts, bringing its metrics in line with long-established television industry measurement standards. Previously, YouTube's view counts have generally reflected individual sessions or devices, but traditional TV measurement has always accounted for the fact that multiple people often watch content together on a single screen, such as a household watching a show as a group. By adopting this co-viewing standard, YouTube's CTV numbers will better reflect actual audience reach rather than just device-level engagement, giving advertisers and content creators a more comparable benchmark against traditional broadcast and cable TV metrics. Importantly, YouTube confirmed this isn't a one-time adjustment limited to CTV: the company plans to apply these updated, co-viewing-inclusive view counts consistently across all its viewing formats moving forward, not just connected television screens. This shift signals YouTube's continued push to position itself as a direct competitor to traditional TV in the eyes of advertisers and media buyers evaluating reach and engagement.
articles.li_summary: YouTube will now report Connected TV view counts using television industry co-viewing standards, meaning multiple people watching the same screen count as separate views, aligning its CTV metrics with traditional TV measurement going forward.

articles.title: TikTok adds new AI transparency and parental controls
articles.summary: At its third Safety and Innovation Summit, TikTok announced a batch of platform updates focused on AI transparency and teen safety. The company detailed new labeling systems designed to flag AI-generated or AI-edited content more clearly, giving viewers better context about how videos were made and helping creators disclose synthetic media use. Alongside this, TikTok expanded its Family Pairing suite, giving parents and guardians more granular controls over teen accounts, including options tied to content exposure, screen time, and messaging settings. The summit also addressed creator protections, with TikTok outlining measures meant to shield creators from misuse of their likeness or content through AI tools, reflecting growing industry pressure around deepfakes and synthetic media misuse. These changes build on TikTok's prior safety initiatives and come as regulators and advocacy groups continue scrutinizing how social platforms handle AI content disclosure and minor protections. The announcements signal TikTok's effort to stay ahead of both regulatory demands and public concern over AI's role in shaping what users see and trust on the platform.
articles.li_summary: TikTok unveiled new AI-content labeling tools and expanded Family Pairing parental controls at its third annual Safety and Innovation Summit, aiming to protect creators and teen users from misleading AI media.

articles.title: Sociable: Instagram adds Amazon affiliate links
articles.summary: Instagram has partnered with Amazon to let creators embed shoppable Amazon product links directly into their Reels, with each Reel supporting up to 30 tagged items. The integration is designed to simplify affiliate marketing by removing the need for creators to direct followers to external links in bios or captions, instead allowing viewers to browse and purchase Amazon products without leaving the Instagram app. This move reflects a broader push by both companies to capture more social commerce revenue, as short-form video continues to drive purchasing decisions among younger audiences. For creators, the feature offers a more direct path to monetization through affiliate commissions tied to Amazon's existing marketplace, while Instagram benefits from keeping users engaged on-platform rather than losing them to outbound links. The partnership signals growing convergence between entertainment content and e-commerce, positioning Reels as a shopping discovery tool alongside its existing role in entertainment and brand marketing, and it gives marketers a new testing ground for product placement strategies within influencer-driven video content.
articles.li_summary: Instagram and Amazon launched a partnership letting creators tag up to 30 shoppable Amazon products directly within a single Reel, streamlining affiliate marketing for social commerce.

articles.title: How SharkNinja is doubling down on its creator strategy
articles.summary: SharkNinja is expanding its creator-driven marketing approach by rolling out two new programs designed to strengthen its social media footprint. One program is aimed at mobilizing employees to act as brand advocates online, encouraging staff to create and share content that amplifies the company's presence across platforms. The second program targets external content creators, formalizing how SharkNinja collaborates with influencers and creators to produce branded content. Together, these initiatives signal the company's continued investment in creator partnerships as a core pillar of its marketing strategy, building on its existing reputation for leveraging social media to drive product awareness and engagement. By tapping both internal employees and external creators, SharkNinja is positioning itself to scale content production, diversify its messaging across audiences, and maintain momentum in an increasingly competitive social commerce landscape where brand authenticity and creator-led storytelling have become key differentiators for consumer product companies.
articles.li_summary: SharkNinja is launching two new initiatives, an employee advocacy program and a content creator program, to expand its social media presence and deepen its influencer marketing strategy.

articles.title: Meta launches shopping platform Achados in Brazil
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out Achados, a shopping platform designed specifically for the Brazilian market, consolidating product listings sourced from across its family of apps—including Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp—into a single, unified marketplace interface. Rather than forcing users to browse separate catalogs on each app, Achados pulls together items from sellers and brands already active on Meta's platforms, presenting them in one centralized discovery hub. The move signals Meta's continued push to strengthen e-commerce capabilities within its ecosystem, giving Brazilian consumers an easier way to search, compare, and shop products without switching between apps, while also creating a more streamlined channel for merchants and advertisers to reach shoppers. Brazil, one of Meta's largest and most engaged markets in Latin America, serves as a strategic testing ground for this kind of integrated commerce feature, reflecting broader industry trends of social platforms blurring the line between content, communication, and online retail as they compete for a larger share of digital shopping activity.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Achados, a new shopping marketplace in Brazil that aggregates product listings from Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp into one unified browsing and discovery experience for users.

articles.title: Threads tests new Q&A option in live chats
articles.summary: Meta's Threads app is piloting a new Q&A format built into its live chat function, giving hosts a structured way to gather questions from participants during a session. Rather than simply reading messages as they appear, hosts will be able to solicit specific questions from the audience, which other chat members can then vote on to determine which get asked first. The feature appears aimed at making live chats more organized and interactive, especially for hosts fielding large volumes of audience input, such as creators, brands, or public figures hosting Q&A sessions. By letting the community prioritize questions through voting, Threads could reduce chat clutter and help hosts focus on the topics generating the most interest. The test is still in an experimental phase, with no confirmed timeline for a broader rollout. If it performs well, this could become a standard tool for live interactions on the platform, giving Threads another point of differentiation as it competes with X and other real-time conversation apps.
articles.li_summary: Threads is testing a Q&A feature within its live chat tool that lets hosts collect audience questions while participants vote on which ones get prioritized and answered.

The platform's main recommendation is that marketers should start their planning process far ahead of the actual event rather than scrambling in the weeks before kickoff. This early-start approach is meant to give brands time to properly map out which subreddits are relevant to their goals, understand the specific tone and culture of those communities, and design engagement strategies that feel native rather than like traditional advertising. articles.li_summary: Reddit released a new guide advising brands to begin planning subreddit engagement strategies for the 2027 Super Bowl well in advance, emphasizing early community mapping over last-minute campaigns.

articles.title: LinkedIn study explores B2B buying decisions
articles.summary: LinkedIn has released research examining how B2B buyers actually make purchasing decisions, and the findings point to the growing weight of relational, trust-based factors over purely transactional ones. Rather than relying solely on product specs, pricing sheets, or sales pitches, business buyers are shown to lean heavily on testimonials from existing customers and validation from industry peers when evaluating vendors. This suggests that traditional B2B marketing tactics focused on feature lists and direct outreach may be less persuasive than content that demonstrates real-world trust, such as case studies, reviews, and peer recommendations. For marketers, the implication is that building credibility through third-party voices and community endorsement could be more effective at moving buyers through the funnel than brand-generated messaging alone. The research reinforces a broader shift in B2B marketing strategy toward relationship-driven and socially validated content, encouraging companies to prioritize cultivating genuine customer advocacy and peer networks as part of their demand generation and conversion efforts, rather than depending on conventional sales collateral to close deals.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn's new research into B2B purchasing behavior finds that relational factors, particularly customer testimonials and peer validation, play a decisive role in shaping client purchase decisions.

articles.title: Paid media now plays largest role in brand-funded creator growth: report
articles.summary: A recent industry report reveals a significant shift in how brands fund creator partnerships, with paid media amplification now accounting for close to half of all brand-funded creator spending. This approach—where companies pay to boost or distribute creator-made content through advertising channels—has overtaken the long-standing #sponsored post model, which simply compensates creators for organic posts to their own audiences. The finding signals that marketers increasingly view creator content as a raw asset to be amplified through paid distribution rather than relying solely on a creator's existing reach and engagement. This trend suggests brands are treating influencer-generated content more like traditional ad creative, optimizing it for performance media placements across social platforms rather than treating it as a one-off endorsement. For marketing professionals, this points to a maturing creator economy where production and amplification strategies are increasingly intertwined, requiring budgets and workflows that blend influencer relationships with paid social expertise rather than keeping these functions separate.
articles.li_summary: A new report finds brands now allocate nearly 50% of creator-marketing budgets to paid media amplification, surpassing traditional sponsored-post deals as the dominant spending category.

articles.title: TikTok releases its 2026 Music Impact Report
articles.summary: TikTok published its 2026 Music Impact Report, highlighting the platform's growing influence over which songs become global hits. The headline finding: 94% of tracks that appeared on the Billboard Global 200 chart in 2025 experienced a viral moment on TikTok before they climbed onto that chart. In practical terms, this means the vast majority of the world's most popular songs last year were propelled by user-generated trends, sounds, challenges, or clips on the app before achieving mainstream chart success through traditional streaming and sales metrics. The finding reinforces TikTok's position as a primary discovery engine for the music industry, effectively acting as an early-warning signal or launchpad for hits well ahead of official chart recognition. For marketers, labels, and artists, the data signals that TikTok virality is increasingly a prerequisite—rather than a byproduct—of commercial music success, making the platform a critical testing ground for new releases and a key metric for predicting which songs are likely to break through to broader audiences and official industry rankings.
articles.li_summary: TikTok's 2026 Music Impact Report found that 94% of songs on the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on the platform before entering the chart, underscoring its outsized role in shaping global hit music.

articles.title: Meta brings its updated Creator Dashboard to the web
articles.summary: Meta has rolled out its newly redesigned Creator Dashboard to the web, extending a tool that was previously limited to mobile app access. This marks another iteration of Meta's creator management console, reflecting the company's ongoing effort to streamline how creators monitor and control their content, audience, and account settings in one place. By bringing the dashboard to desktop, Meta is making it easier for creators who prefer working on larger screens or managing multiple accounts to access analytics, content controls, and other creator-focused features without relying solely on mobile devices. The move signals Meta's broader push to position this dashboard as the default, unified starting point for creator operations, phasing out older, fragmented management interfaces in favor of a single consistent experience across both mobile and web platforms.
articles.li_summary: Meta has expanded its redesigned Creator Dashboard to desktop web access, positioning it as the primary control panel for managing creator presence across its apps, replacing older in-app management tools.

articles.title: Snapchat adds more creator partnership opportunities
articles.summary: Snapchat is piloting two new features aimed at expanding creator-brand collaboration on the app. The first is a revamped version of its Snap Creator Network, a platform designed to connect creators with brands for sponsored content and partnership opportunities, though Snapchat has not detailed exactly what changes are being tested. The second addition, "Visited By" listings, will appear on Snap Map and highlight which creators have visited specific locations, such as restaurants, stores, or events, giving local businesses a new way to showcase influencer engagement and attract foot traffic. Together, these tools suggest Snapchat is leaning further into creator commerce and local marketing, positioning itself as a platform where creators can monetize visits and collaborations while brands gain visibility through authentic, location-based content. Marketers watching the creator economy should note this as another signal that social platforms are building more structured, discoverable ways to match creators with business opportunities tied to real-world locations.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat is testing an updated Snap Creator Network alongside new "Visited By" listings on Snap Map, giving brands and local businesses fresh ways to connect with creators for promotional partnerships.

articles.title: Snapchat enables Lens creation via third-party AI tools
articles.summary: Snapchat has rolled out a new tool called Easy Lens, a command line interface designed to simplify how creators build AR Lenses for the platform. Instead of requiring developers to work exclusively within Snap's native Lens Studio environment, Easy Lens allows them to connect their chatbot of choice, including popular third-party AI assistants, to generate and refine Lens code through conversational prompts. This approach lowers the technical barrier for Lens creation, letting creators describe the effect they want in natural language and have the AI handle much of the coding work behind the scenes. By opening up compatibility to external AI tools rather than locking developers into a single proprietary system, Snap is betting that flexibility will encourage more creators, including those without deep AR or coding backgrounds, to experiment with building Lenses. The move reflects a broader industry trend of platforms integrating AI-assisted development tools to accelerate content creation and reduce production friction for creators and brands alike.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat introduced a new Easy Lens command line interface that lets developers build AR Lenses by pairing it with any third-party AI chatbot they prefer, rather than relying solely on Snap's own tools.

articles.title: LinkedIn adds ninth in-stream game
articles.summary: LinkedIn has rolled out Sumbreak, a new math-based puzzle game, becoming the ninth in-stream game added to the professional networking platform. The addition continues LinkedIn's strategy of incorporating casual gaming content directly into the user feed as a tool to drive higher retention and deeper engagement among its member base. By offering quick, skill-based puzzles like Sumbreak alongside its existing lineup of in-app games, LinkedIn aims to give users another reason to open the app daily and spend more time interacting with the platform beyond professional networking, job searching, and content browsing. This move reflects a broader trend among social and professional platforms turning to lightweight gaming experiences to compete for user attention in a crowded digital landscape. While specific performance metrics for Sumbreak have not been disclosed, its launch signals LinkedIn's continued investment in gamification as part of its product roadmap to keep users returning to the platform more frequently throughout the week.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn launched Sumbreak, a math-based puzzle, marking its ninth in-stream game as the platform continues expanding casual gaming features to boost user retention and daily engagement.

articles.title: Holiday marketing hits inflection point in 2026: What brands need to know
articles.summary: As marketers begin shaping 2026 holiday campaigns, a central challenge has emerged around balancing emerging AI-powered tools with proven tactics like influencer and creator collaborations. Consumers are showing a push-pull dynamic: they're increasingly skeptical of heavily automated or AI-generated marketing content, questioning its authenticity and relevance, while still responding positively to creator-led campaigns that feel personal and trustworthy. This creates pressure for brands to avoid over-indexing on flashy AI applications purely for novelty's sake, since doing so risks alienating holiday shoppers who want genuine, relatable messaging during a high-spend season. At the same time, creator partnerships remain a reliable driver of engagement and conversion, giving brands a dependable channel even as the broader marketing landscape shifts toward more automated, data-driven approaches. The takeaway for marketing teams is that success in the 2026 holiday season will hinge on thoughtful integration rather than wholesale replacement—using AI to support efficiency and personalization behind the scenes while keeping human-driven creator content front and center in consumer-facing campaigns to maintain trust and authenticity.
articles.li_summary: Brands planning 2026 holiday campaigns face a growing tension between consumers' wariness of AI-driven marketing tactics and their continued trust in creator partnerships, forcing marketers to recalibrate their strategic mix.

articles.title: Snapchat shares insight into luxury shopping trends
articles.summary: Snapchat has released findings from a newly commissioned study examining how its user base engages with luxury brands and products. The headline finding shows that 84% of Snapchat users report that social media platforms make them feel more connected to the world of luxury goods, suggesting these apps are becoming a meaningful touchpoint for premium brand exposure rather than just casual browsing or entertainment destinations. This data point signals to marketers that platforms like Snapchat are increasingly viewed by their audiences as gateways into aspirational shopping categories traditionally reserved for in-store experiences or glossy print campaigns. For luxury brands evaluating where to allocate advertising budgets, this kind of consumer sentiment research offers justification for deeper investment in social-first campaigns targeting younger, digitally native shoppers who may not frequent traditional luxury retail channels but still desire connection to high-end products through their everyday social feeds and interactions.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat's new commissioned study found that 84% of its users feel social media platforms bring them closer to the luxury goods universe, highlighting the app's growing role in premium brand discovery.

articles.title: Meta launches messaging app for teens
articles.summary: Meta has introduced a new standalone app called Direct, aimed at giving teen users a separate space for Instagram direct messages instead of keeping that function bundled inside the main Instagram app. The move echoes an almost identical attempt Meta made in 2017, when it first tested a dedicated Direct messaging app before quietly dropping the idea. By spinning messaging out into its own product again, Meta appears to be revisiting that earlier strategy, likely betting that younger users prefer a lighter, chat-focused experience separate from Instagram's feed, Stories, and Reels. The app keeps the core DM experience intact, letting users send messages, photos, and other content just as they would through Instagram itself, but positions it as a standalone download rather than a feature buried inside a larger platform. For marketers and brands tracking youth engagement, this signals Meta's continued effort to court teen audiences through simplified, single-purpose apps, following similar moves by competitors building separate messaging-first products.
articles.li_summary: Meta has relaunched Direct, a standalone messaging app that splits Instagram DMs into their own platform, mirroring a nearly identical app the company briefly tried back in 2017.

articles.title: Pinterest shares its first Creators to Watch list
articles.summary: Pinterest has released its first-ever "Creators to Watch" list, naming 20 influencers from around the world identified as rising voices for 2027. The initiative marks a new effort by the platform to formally recognize creator talent likely to shape trends and engagement in the coming years, rather than focusing solely on current top performers. For brands and marketers, the list functions as an early scouting tool, offering a curated starting point for identifying creators who may deliver strong returns on partnership investment before they become mainstream picks. Since Pinterest has increasingly positioned itself as a discovery and inspiration platform for shopping and lifestyle content, the creators featured likely span categories such as fashion, home design, beauty, and DIY, aligning with the platform's core audience behavior. By publishing this list, Pinterest is also signaling its ambition to compete more directly with other platforms' creator economies, giving brands a reason to deepen their presence on Pinterest through early, strategic creator collaborations rather than waiting until these influencers reach broader recognition elsewhere.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest unveiled its inaugural "Creators to Watch" list, spotlighting 20 global influencers positioned for growth in 2027, giving brands early signals on which creators to prioritize for future partnerships.

articles.title: Snapchat will show more info on mutual friends
articles.summary: Snapchat is introducing a new opt-in privacy feature that reveals mutual friends between users right on their profile pages. Instead of having to guess or ask around about shared connections, users who choose to enable this setting will be able to see a visible list of friends they have in common with anyone they view. The feature is designed to make it easier to verify who someone is connected to before adding them, which could reduce friend requests from unfamiliar accounts and build more trust within the app's social graph. Because it requires users to actively opt in, Snapchat is framing this as a privacy-conscious update rather than a default change, giving people control over whether their mutual connections are shared publicly. The rollout reflects a broader trend among social apps to surface relationship context that helps users navigate who to trust and connect with, similar to mutual-friend features already common on platforms like Facebook and LinkedIn, though Snapchat has not detailed a specific release timeline.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat is rolling out an opt-in feature that lets users see a list of mutual friends displayed directly on another person's profile, making shared connections visible instantly.

articles.title: Meta expands content protection to Instagram
articles.summary: Meta announced it is bringing its existing Facebook content protection system to Instagram, giving creators on both platforms the same safeguards against unauthorized reposting of their work. The system relies on automatic detection technology that scans for matches to a creator's original content across the platform, then sends an alert when a repost is identified. This mirrors the tool Meta already uses on Facebook, where creators receive notifications if someone else shares their video or photo without permission, helping them track where their content is being redistributed and take action if needed. By extending this feature to Instagram, Meta is aiming to give creators more visibility and control over how their content spreads across its family of apps, addressing a long-standing concern among creators about losing credit or engagement when their posts are copied and reshared by other accounts without attribution.
articles.li_summary: Meta is extending its Facebook content protection tools to Instagram, using automatic detection to alert original creators whenever their videos or photos get reposted by other accounts.
